editorial.editorial_title: Drawing hair with whole-body strokes, rhythm, references, and revision
editorial.summary: A 6:52 tutorial that uses Emeril Lagasse’s Bam persona to transform a stick figure through whole-arm/body hair strokes. It moves through shading/highlights, bun/Princess Leia, starburst, ponytail, Mohawk/Kid ’n Play, strays, Medusa and Jennifer Aniston/Friends feathering while invoking The Cure, sword/nunchuck movement, leg-day/off-balance/no-rhythm self-critique, gendered shave-head/grow-long-hair advice, Vidal Sassoon/product/paycheck jokes, and drawing-level haircut/scissors/hat recovery. Four damaged phrases remain unresolved. Every idea remains without becoming ergonomic, exercise, weapon, gender, hair-care or scissor guidance.

The speaker references walls/streets, but the detailed phrase is damaged.
Whole arm/body/shoulder motion drives hair strokes.
The Cure and imagined rhythm cue movement.
Swords and nunchucks describe gestures, not use instructions.
Princess Leia, Kid n Play, Medusa and Jennifer Aniston index changing forms.
No-soul/no-rhythm insult is immediately called not nice.
The speaker explicitly labels shave/grow suggestions as masculinity advice.
Too much hair becomes haircut, reset and hat rather than a mistake.
